title: Google may spend $1.5bn on a 35-person startup to catch up on AI coding

content_html:
Google wants its AI to code better. It may have found a shortcut, and it runs through a startup of about 35 people.

The company is in talks with Mechanize, a San Francisco startup that trains AI agents to write software, Business Insider reported. The deal would be worth more than $1.5 billion, four people familiar with the talks said. It is still in progress, and the terms could change.

What Google would get is narrower than an acquisition. It would hire some of Mechanize’s staff and take a non-exclusive licence to its technology. The recruits would work on evaluating and developing Google’s models. Both companies declined to comment.

Why $1.5bn for 35 people

Mechanize is barely a year old. Three former researchers from Epoch AI, an institute that measures how capable models are, launched it in April 2025. Its chief executive, Tamay Besiroglu, co-founded Epoch. Earlier this year the startup said it had raised $9.1 million at a $500 million valuation, with backers including former GitHub chief Nat Friedman, Stripe’s Patrick Collison, and the podcaster Dwarkesh Patel.

Its stated mission is blunt: automate every job. It started with software because code can be graded.

That grading is the actual product. Coding agents learn inside training environments. Each one is a prompt, a working codebase, and a grader that decides whether the agent did the job. Those environments feed reinforcement learning and model evaluations. RuntimeWire reports that one engineer builds each task from idea to grading. That takes about a week. Most of the effort goes into making the grader fair, consistent, and hard for a model to cheat.

That is what Google is paying for. Not a consumer product, but the judgement to find where frontier coding models fail and build fair tests around it. A licence buys the finished work. Hiring the people keeps it coming as the models improve.

The playbook, again

Google has run this move before. Rather than buy a startup outright, it hires the key staff and licenses the technology. The structure sidesteps the antitrust scrutiny a full takeover attracts.

In July 2025 it took the Windsurf founders and a non-exclusive licence to their coding tool, a package reported at about $2.4 billion. Varun Mohan, Windsurf’s chief executive, now runs Google’s Antigravity coding platform. In 2024 Google rehired the Character AI co-founder Noam Shazeer and paid for rights to that startup’s technology. Shazeer has since left for OpenAI.

The Mechanize talks push the same playbook further down the supply chain. Windsurf gave Google a product developers use. Mechanize would give it the machinery to train the models underneath.

The timing is brutal

The deal surfaced in a bad week for Google’s AI. Days earlier, DeepMind boss Demis Hassabis stepped back and the chief scientist, Jeff Dean, left to start his own company. Google shares fell around 4% on that news. The lab had already been under visible strain over talent and delays.

The coding gap is the backdrop. Google’s flagship Gemini has slipped repeatedly on coding, while OpenAI and Anthropic pulled developers onto Codex and Claude Code. The fight has moved from the model to the tools around it, and rivals are building their own. Meta just launched its own coding agent. Buying Mechanize’s evaluation craft is a way to close the distance without waiting for the next Gemini.

What the headline number hides

The $1.5 billion figure needs care. RuntimeWire notes it is the value of the whole arrangement, not a purchase price or a fresh valuation. The money could be split across licensing fees, salaries, founders, and investors, leaving a smaller Mechanize still standing. Deedy Das called the talks an acquisition on X, but the underlying report describes a licence-and-hire deal that leaves the company independent.

There is a sharper reading doing the rounds. Google wrote the paper that started the large language model era, then lost the lead to OpenAI. Wccftech points to the awkward symmetry. Apple pays Google roughly $1 billion a year to use Gemini. Google may now pay $1.5 billion to a 35-person shop to make Gemini better at a job its rivals have already nailed.

For now it is talks, not a deal, and the number could move. But the direction is clear. The scarce thing in AI coding is no longer the model. It is the people who can build the tests it keeps failing.

content_html_zh:
谷歌希望其人工智能能够更好地编码。 它可能找到了一条捷径，它贯穿于一家大约 35 人的初创公司。

据《商业内幕》报道，该公司正在与旧金山一家培训人工智能代理编写软件的初创公司 Mechanize 进行谈判。 四位知情人士表示，这笔交易的价值将超过 15 亿美元。 该项目仍在进行中，条款可能会发生变化。

谷歌所能得到的范围比收购要窄。 它将雇用 Mechanize 的一些员工，并获得其技术的非独家许可。 新员工将致力于评估和开发谷歌的模型。 两家公司均拒绝置评。

为什么 35 人需要 15 亿美元

机械化还不到一年的历史。 Epoch AI（一家测量模型能力的研究所）的三名前研究人员于 2025 年 4 月推出了该项目。 其首席执行官 Tamay Besiroglu 是 Epoch 的联合创始人。 今年早些时候，这家初创公司表示已以 5 亿美元的估值筹集了 910 万美元，支持者包括 GitHub 前首席执行官 Nat Friedman、Stripe 的 Patrick Collison 和播客 Dwarkesh Patel。

它宣称的使命很直白：自动化每项工作。 它从软件开始，因为代码可以分级。

该分级是实际产品。 编码代理在训练环境中学习。 每一个都是一个提示、一个工作代码库和一个评分器，用于决定代理是否完成了工作。 这些环境为强化学习和模型评估提供支持。 RuntimeWire 报告称，每项任务从构思到评分均由一位工程师负责构建。 这需要大约一周的时间。 大部分的努力都花在让评分者公平、一致，并且模型难以作弊。

这就是谷歌付出的代价。 不是消费产品，而是找到前沿编码模型失败之处并围绕其构建公平测试的判断。 许可证可以购买已完成的作品。 随着模型的改进，招聘人员的数量不断增加。

又是剧本

谷歌之前就曾采取过这一举措。 它不是直接收购一家初创公司，而是雇佣关键员工并获得技术许可。 该结构避开了全面收购所吸引的反垄断审查。

2025 年 7 月，Windsurf 创始人获得了其编码工具的非独家许可，据称价值约 24 亿美元。 Windsurf 首席执行官瓦伦·莫汉 (Varun Mohan) 现在负责运营谷歌的反重力编码平台。 2024 年，谷歌重新聘用了 Character AI 联合创始人诺姆·沙泽尔 (Noam Shazeer)，并支付了该初创公司技术的使用权。 Shazeer 此后离开前往 OpenAI。

机械化谈判将同样的剧本进一步推向供应链。 Windsurf 为 Google 提供了开发人员使用的产品。 机械化将为它提供训练下面模型的机器。

时机是残酷的

这笔交易的出现正值谷歌人工智能业务表现不佳的一周。 几天前，DeepMind 老板德米斯·哈萨比斯 (Demis Hassabis) 辞职，首席科学家杰夫·迪恩 (Jeff Dean) 离职，创办了自己的公司。 受此消息影响，谷歌股价下跌约 4%。 该实验室已经明显面临人才短缺和延误的压力。

编码差距是背景。 谷歌的旗舰产品 Gemini 在编码方面屡次下滑，而 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 将开发人员吸引到了 Codex 和 Claude Code 上。 斗争已经从模型转向了围绕模型的工具，竞争对手正在构建自己的工具。 Meta 刚刚推出了自己的编码代理。 购买 Mechanize 的评估船是一种拉近距离的方法，无需等待下一个 Gemini。

标题数字隐藏了什么

15 亿美元的数字需要小心谨慎。 RuntimeWire 指出，这是整个安排的价值，而不是购买价格或新估值。 这笔钱可以分配给许可费、工资、创始人和投资者，让规模较小的 Mechanize 继续存在。 Deedy Das 称这次谈判是对 X 的收购，但基础报告描述了一项使该公司独立的许可和雇用交易。

到处都有更清晰的阅读。 谷歌写的论文开启了大语言模型时代，然后输给了 OpenAI。 Wccftech 指出了这种尴尬的对称性。 苹果每年向谷歌支付大约 10 亿美元来使用 Gemini。 谷歌现在可能会向一家拥有 35 名员工的商店支付 15 亿美元，以使 Gemini 更好地完成其竞争对手已经完成的工作。

目前只是谈判，而不是达成协议，而且数字可能会发生变化。 但方向是明确的。 人工智能编码中稀缺的东西不再是模型。 是那些能够构建它不断失败的测试的人。
